tagline: Up the Row River from the Covered Bridge Capital of Oregon.
intro: Out of Cottage Grove, known as the Covered Bridge Capital of Oregon, the road follows the Row River east and goes around Dorena Lake, with a covered bridge near either end. The river's name rhymes with cow, and it comes from a row between two brothers-in-law over trespassing livestock that ended with one of them dead.

The full tour counts seven bridges, and several stand nearer town, off the lake road. Among them are Mosby Creek, built in 1920, the oldest in Lane County and still open to traffic, and the Chambers railroad bridge of 1925 in Cottage Grove.
season: TripCheck lists it as a year-round drive.

moments.title: Currin Bridge
moments.text: Built in 1925 to replace a bridge of 1883, it is the only covered bridge in Oregon painted two colors, white at the portals and red along the sides.

moments.title: Dorena Bridge
moments.text: Built in 1949 after the dam made the lake, it once tied together the roads on either shore and, closed to traffic now, has become a place for weddings.

moments.title: Dorena
moments.text: The town was abandoned in 1946 for the dam, its hundred or so homes were moved before the reservoir covered the old site, and Dorena started over five miles upriver.
